text:
Lin: Flagging a small but important ambiguity: our docs say runtime may "fallback" across hosting modes during overload, but we never defined the observable error contract for callers. We need a terse error shape and header invariant.

Hari: Agreed. What ambiguity are you seeing in practice?

Lin: Twofold: 1) SDKs treat 5xx as retryable and will hit hosted endpoints if fallback was silent. 2) dashboards can't separate intentional warm-failovers from policy-blocked failures.

Jo: Proposed contract: when fallback happens intentionally, router returns 200 with header X-RW-Serving-Mode set to the actual mode used. When fallback is blocked by tenant policy, return 409 + JSON {"code":"FALLBACK_BLOCKED","message":"hosting policy prevents fallback"}.

Priya: I like explicit 200+header for allowed fallbacks. We should also include X-RW-Rollout and X-RW-Attempt to help correlate.

Hari: Also add span tag hosting.mode on root span. If hosting.mode differs from X-RW-Serving-Mode mid-request, emit audit log event and a metric hosting.mode_flip=1.

Lin: Backwards compat: for older clients that don't understand the header, we should log an audit metric and not rely on SDKs. We'll also publish a migration window in the RFC.

Jo: Test plan: unit tests for error shape, integration test that simulates dedicated pool saturation and asserts we either see 200+header or 409+code for private tenants. Add a small chaos test for header mutation to ensure audit events fire.

BuildBot: CI: integration job queued: https://ci.internal/job/arch-contracts/4801234567 

Priya: One more: ensure the 409 body is safe for PII rules. No tenant ids in message. Use log-only tenant id with redaction token.

Lin: OK. I'll draft the RFC with the exact header names and error JSON, include rollout timeline and the audit metric names. Thanks folks.
